skill.name: budget-pacing-monitor
skill.description: Monitors live paid advertising spend against a target budget curve and flags pacing, delivery, and reallocation triggers.
skill.summary: Check whether an active paid campaign is on pace, ahead, behind, or stalled.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backticks, GitHub homepage metadata, or repository-relative documentation links. I confirmed risk where the skill tells agents to run ledger commands and save files using a user-provided campaign name. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Ledger command uses a user-provided campaign placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured argument passing, quote all arguments, and validate campaign names before invoking ledger.py.

remediation.issue: Saved pacing filenames include the campaign name.
remediation.suggestion: Slugify campaign names, reject path separators, and resolve the final path inside memory/ad/budget-pacing-monitor before writing.

remediation.issue: Several links traverse outside the skill folder.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle required references with the skill or replace upward relative links with plain source names.

content.value_statement: Paid campaigns can spend too quickly, too slowly, or stall before teams notice. This skill compares live spend to a target curve and flags action triggers.
actual_capabilities: Compares cumulative spend against an even, front-loaded, or back-loaded target curve.
Labels campaigns as on-track, ahead, behind, or stalled.
Checks learning-phase status before recommending any pacing action.
Identifies likely delivery drivers from exported campaign data.
Creates a pacing summary with budget, flight window, trigger, and next check date.
limitations: Requires user-provided campaign exports or budget details to produce reliable pacing reads.
Does not choose the initial budget allocation or bid strategy.
Does not connect to ad platforms unless the host supplies optional connectors.
Projection quality depends on current spend stability and available daily history.

use_cases.title: Weekly Campaign Pacing Review
use_cases.description: Compare current spend with the planned curve before a weekly budget meeting.

use_cases.title: Mid-Flight Spike Investigation
use_cases.description: Check whether a sudden spend increase reflects over-delivery, cap pressure, or normal pacing.

use_cases.title: Reallocation Trigger Handoff
use_cases.description: Document when a campaign has crossed the pacing band and needs budget review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Pacing Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with budget and elapsed days.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check pacing for Campaign A. The daily budget is $200, and we are 9 days into a 30-day flight.

prompt_templates.title: Flight Curve Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the campaign has a stated spend curve.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pacing for this export using a front-loaded curve. Budget is $15,000, flight is June 1 to June 30.

prompt_templates.title: Spike Or Stall Diagnosis
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when spend changed suddenly during the flight.
prompt_templates.prompt: Spend jumped two days ago and the daily cap is hit by noon. Decide whether this campaign is ahead of pace.

prompt_templates.title: Reallocation Trigger Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review with learning status and handoff needs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the export to calculate percent-to-pace, check learning status, name the driver, and decide whether the reallocation trigger fires.

output_examples.input: Campaign X has spent 30 percent of budget after 60 percent of the flight.
output_examples.output: The campaign is behind pace. It needs driver review before any budget move, especially learning status and recent serving volume.

output_examples.input: A daily budget campaign hits its cap before noon for three straight days.
output_examples.output: The campaign is likely ahead of pace. The report should separate measured cap pressure from the projected end-of-flight overspend.

output_examples.input: A campaign is inside its pacing band but remains in learning phase.
output_examples.output: The trigger should hold. The pacing note should mark the read as observational until learning exits.

best_practices: Set the target curve before reviewing spend data.
Use exported daily spend, budget, flight dates, and delivery status when available.
Label each figure as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
anti_patterns: Do not infer daily pacing from a single dashboard screenshot.
Do not reallocate budget while the campaign is still in learning phase.
Do not treat projected end-of-flight spend as measured spend.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs budget, flight dates, elapsed time, target curve, spend history, and delivery status when available.

faq.question: Can it choose a new budget?
faq.answer: No. It identifies whether reallocation should be considered and hands the actual allocation decision to another skill.

faq.question: Does it require ad platform API access?
faq.answer: No. Manual campaign exports are enough. Optional connectors can help when the host environment supports them.

faq.question: How does it handle learning phase?
faq.answer: It reports pacing but holds reallocation triggers until learning has exited.

faq.question: What target curves are supported?
faq.answer: It supports even, front-loaded, and back-loaded pacing curves.

faq.question: Is this useful for one-day campaigns?
faq.answer: It is less useful for very short flights because daily variance can dominate the pacing signal.
